purpose: Phase-5A TARGET ENGAGEMENT registry - the first pharmacology layer. Defines ONLY molecular recognition: schematic molecular targets, drug-target encounter, reversible/irreversible binding, occupancy, saturation, competition, residence time, and affinity metrics (Kd/Ki/IC50) WHEN evidence exists. It is a SEPARATE layer that READS the intracellular/uptake outputs read-only and modifies nothing upstream. NOTHING downstream of target binding is defined (no signalling, phosphorylation, MAPK/PI3K/AKT/mTOR/NF-kB, gene regulation, transcription, translation, apoptosis, proliferation, immune response, toxicity, efficacy, PK, PD downstream, tumour response).
authoritative_source: data/profile-b-evidence-package.json (FROZEN). Chen 2012 reports skin permeation, cellular uptake and in-vivo melanoma pharmacodynamics but NO molecular target identity or binding constants (Kd/Ki/IC50, kon/koff) for tripterine. Shukla 2020 'binding affinity' is celastrol-cyclodextrin COMPLEXATION, not a protein target. So target identity + binding are NOT REPORTED for this formulation; no target values are fabricated, and no outside knowledge is used to fill the gap.

prediction_labels.note: A prediction is acceptable ONLY when explicitly labelled; never presented as an experimental fact.
prediction_labels.HIGH_CONFIDENCE_PREDICTION: strongly supported prediction (close analogue / robust model)
prediction_labels.LITERATURE_PREDICTION: prediction derived from separate literature (not this formulation)

target_types.note: Generic schematic molecular TARGETS (individual proteins) - NOT cells or organelles. No disease-specific assumptions.

binding_models.note: Occupancy/dissociation/residence time supported for both. Irreversible never dissociates.

affinity_metrics.note: Kd/Ki/IC50 are shown ONLY when evidence exists; otherwise Prediction or Not Reported. Numeric values are never fabricated. residence_time = 1/koff; Kd = koff/kon.

formulations.note: Per-formulation target profile (registry data; never hard-coded). For B1 the molecular target is NOT REPORTED (no target identity or binding constants in the frozen package), so no targets are placed and the engagement layer is idle. kon/koff/Kd are never invented.

binding.basis: No molecular target identity or binding constants are reported for tripterine in the frozen package; nothing is fabricated and no outside knowledge is used.

species_target.note: Per-species target-engagement evidence. NOT REPORTED for all species (no target/binding data for this formulation); no fabricated evidence; no rat->human copy.

rat.message: Target Engagement Evidence: Not Reported. No molecular target or binding constants are reported for this formulation; no binding is shown.

human.message: Target Engagement Evidence: Not Reported. No molecular target or binding constants are reported for this formulation; no binding is shown.

mouse.message: Target Engagement Evidence: Not Reported. No molecular target or binding constants are reported for this formulation; no binding is shown.

integrity.reads_only: The target-engagement engine READS the intracellular/uptake outputs read-only and modifies NOTHING upstream. Binding state lives only in this engine (the Phase-4D molecule is never changed).
integrity.encounter_only: Binding begins ONLY after a drug molecule physically reaches a target's vicinity. No long-distance attraction, no teleportation.
integrity.occupancy_capacity: Occupied sites never exceed a target's available sites; excess molecules keep diffusing (competition).
integrity.irreversible_no_dissociation: Irreversible binding never dissociates; only reversible binding may dissociate (koff).
integrity.nuclear_gate: Binding a nuclear target requires that Phase-4D nucleus targeting has occurred (the drug has reached the nuclear membrane).
integrity.ends_at: Ends at target binding / occupancy / (optional) dissociation. Nothing downstream.

provenance_sources: data/profile-b-evidence-package.json (FROZEN) - no molecular target identity or binding constants for tripterine; in-vivo PD is downstream (not modelled here)
Chen Y et al. Int J Nanomedicine 2012;7:3023-3033 (DOI 10.2147/IJN.S32476) - primary full-text source
